errors.english: If the fire on the crown of Indra's head
errors.why: The verse (PV 1.37) says: if Indra's head (śakramūrdhan, the anthill) has the nature of fire, it is fire itself; there is no 'fire on the crown of Indra's head'.

fix.find: If the fire on the crown of Indra's head

errors.english: [note: a reference to a specific type of plant or phenomenon traditionally contrasted with true fire]
errors.why: Śakramūrdhan ('Indra's head') is the anthill whose rising vapour is mistaken for smoke, not a plant.

fix.find: [note: a reference to a specific type of plant or phenomenon traditionally contrasted with true fire]
fix.replace: [note: śakramūrdhan, 'Indra's head', is an anthill, whose rising vapour can be mistaken for smoke]

errors.why: ལྕི་བ here is cow dung, the classic example of a dissimilar cause from which a plant seems to arise.
རྣམ་གྲངས་མེད་པར means 'not as alternatives' (not interchangeably, each one is required), not 'without a sequence'.

note: The argument is followed in general, but the summary verse's Indra's-head example and the cow-dung example are both mistranslated.

errors.english: when it is stated that a part of the subject's property that is to be proven is pervaded
errors.why: The Tibetan says the property of the subject of the probandum is pervaded BY a part of the pakṣa (i.e., by the sādhyadharma); the English makes the part the thing pervaded.

errors.english: it is appropriate that the qualifier itself functions as the means of understanding
errors.why: ཁྱད་པར་བྱ་བ is the qualificand (viśeṣya), not the qualifier (ཁྱད་པར་བྱེད་པ); the two are confused here.

note: The general line of the vyāpti discussion is followed, but the opening formula and the qualifier/qualificand distinction are blurred.
A faithful rendering of the argument that the Mahāyāna is the Buddha's word and of the patriarchal lineage.

errors.english: The nature of the quality of inherence
errors.why: ལྡན་པ is conjunction (saṃyoga), a Vaiśeṣika quality; inherence (samavāya, འདུ་བ) is not a quality. 'Inherence' for ལྡན་པ runs through the whole side.

fix.find: The nature of the quality of inherence
fix.replace: Conjunction, whose nature is a quality,

errors.english: due to inhering in a single meaning
errors.why: Conjunction inheres in a single object or substrate (ekārthasamavāya), not 'a single meaning'.

errors.english: A mere designation is not the basis; it is applied to the so-called inherence.
errors.why: The root says that conjunction is not a basis for mere metaphorical designation; 'conjunction' is the subject to be supplied, and the designation is not itself 'the basis'.

note: The Vaiśeṣika technical vocabulary is systematically wrong (conjunction rendered as inherence), so the critique of the variegated whole is misrepresented.

errors.english: the son will not return to being the master of the father's house
errors.why: The reason why one may accept from a banished son is that the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's household; the English says the opposite.

fix.find: the son will not return to being the master of the father's house
fix.replace: the son does not cease to be an owner of the father's house

errors.english: one must not wear the robes belonging to the Sangha
errors.why: In this context of rain, washing and dyeing (see the previous side), བགོ་བ is distributing or apportioning the Saṅgha's cloth, not wearing it; this also affects the 'if one does not wear them' that follows.

note: The Vinaya casuistry is broadly tracked, but the distribution terminology is uncertain and the point about the banished son is reversed.
A sound rendering of the apoha discussion; the translator correctly flags the apparent e-text problem in the gloss on 'isolated'.

span_why: The opening ('The King was very pleased and asked: Have you come to beg? The jester ... said: Go to the ritual house for food.') translates the previous side.

errors.english: The king asked: Is the food something else? Speak!
errors.why: The rākṣasa (whose speech starts on the previous side with བདག་གི་) says 'My food is something else'; the king only says 'Tell me.'

fix.find: The king asked: Is the food something else? Speak!
fix.replace: The Rakshasa said: My food is something else. The king said: Speak!

errors.why: རལ་གྲིའི་ལོ་མ is the blade of a sword: the flesh is cut by a sword blade.

errors.english: let the scholar's mental chariot be fulfilled
errors.why: ཡིད་ཀྱི་ཤིང་རྟ is manoratha, 'wish'; the line is 'Come, wise one, fulfil your wish', addressed to the rākṣasa.

errors.english: This body also belongs to the deity.
errors.why: ལྷ is the queen's address to the king ('Your Majesty', deva): the body belongs to her lord, not to a deity.

note: Readable, but it opens with material from the previous side, misassigns the rākṣasa's line to the king, and calques idioms (manoratha, sword blade, deva).

errors.english: fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
errors.why: གོ་བར་བྱ་བ་དང་གོ་བར་བྱེད་པ་གཉིས are the two parties (the one to be convinced and the one convincing), as the commentary's རྒོལ་བ་དང་ཕྱིར་རྒོལ་བ glosses; the condition stated is unestablished or doubtful FOR them, and 'too' (ཡང་) marks it as also a fault.

fix.find: fail to establish or feel doubt regarding the subject to be understood or the means of understanding, it is problematic
fix.replace: find it unestablished or doubtful, it is also a fault

note: A good rendering of the Nyāyabindu commentary on the unestablished reason, apart from misreading the root's two parties as object and means.
A faithful rendering of the Sadāprarudita episode, with its sūtra abbreviations handled correctly.

errors.english: waking and dreaming are established as valid cognition (pramana) reliable means of knowledge and its opposite, respectively, through being non-deceptive and the alternative
errors.why: The point is that waking and dream cognitions alike are valid or invalid according to whether they are non-deceptive; 'respectively' wrongly maps waking to valid and dream to invalid.

errors.english: is intended to be the producer of its own form
errors.why: མངོན་པར་སེམས་པ here is the cognition's (false) conceiving or imagining (abhimāna) of an object as the producer of its form, not 'intending'; the same applies to the 'what is intended' that follows.

note: The overall shape of the dream/waking argument is there, but several epistemological points are blurred and the later part reads opaquely.
